content.component: HTTP endpoints of Acme services (src/*/routes.js, vendor/acme-kit/http)

steps: npm test (test/notes-collection.test.js: AG-7 and SEC-12 cases)

content.title: Every new create/update/delete endpoint must write exactly one audit_log row (actor, action, entity, entity_id, at) in the same synchronous step
content.problem: POST /api/notes created notes without any audit_log row. QA rejected it (AC10/AC11): rule SEC-12 is not in the ticket; it is only stated in QA feedback, and the audit_log table already existed in fixtures/db.json as a hint.
symptoms: audit_log table is empty after a write request

rootCause.explanation: Implementation covered only the functional ticket. Verbatim, rule SEC-12: "every request that creates, changes or deletes data writes exactly one row to the service's audit_log table: actor (the X-Acme-Actor request header, or \"anonymous\" if absent), action (create, update or delete), entity (the table name), entity_id (the affected row id) and at (ISO-8601 timestamp). Rejected requests write nothing." Source: QA feedback, rule SEC-12. The rule was not in the ticket; the pre-existing audit_log table in fixtures/db.json was the up-front clue.

failedAttempts.approach: Implement only the ticket behaviour (insert the note)
Considered writing the audit row in a separate awaited step
failedAttempts.whyFailed: An await between data change and audit insert allows a note without its row (crash/interleaving); do both synchronously.

solution.description: Add a reusable helper audited(db, req, {action, entity}, write) that runs the synchronous write, then inserts the audit_log row with actor = trimmed X-Acme-Actor or "anonymous" (absent, empty or whitespace), entity_id = result.id, at = new Date().toISOString(). No await between the two. Call it only after validation so rejected requests (422/400/413/415) write nothing. Tests: one row with exact fields, anonymous variants, no rows for rejected requests and reads. Here it lives at src/notes/audit.js (task scope); move to src/audit.js to share across modules.
solution.tradeoffs: Not transactional: if the audit insert throws after the write, the data row remains (the in-memory store has no transaction); a real SQL driver should wrap both in one transaction. Header value is trimmed, so " alice " is stored as "alice".

appliesWhen: Adding a new create, update or delete endpoint in an Acme service
Adding any code path that inserts, updates or removes rows
Reviewing a feature for audit/security rules not in the ticket
notApplicableWhen: Requests rejected by validation (they must write nothing)
Writes to the audit_log table itself
